commands.name: project_new
commands.description: Makes a new Xcode project from a template (File > New > Project…) in a folder; Xcode makes folder/name/name.xcodeproj and opens it.

args.name: name
args.meaning: The product name; also the new folder's name.

args.name: folder
args.meaning: The existing folder to make it in, an absolute path or one starting with ~.

args.name: template
args.meaning: The template's name as Xcode shows it; only App was verified.

args.name: organization
args.meaning: The Organization Identifier, a reverse-DNS prefix.

args.name: git
args.meaning: Whether Xcode makes a Git repository; only False was verified.

example_requests: Create a new iOS app project called MyApp in Documents/XcodeProjects
Start a macOS app in Xcode
commands.precondition: The program has Accessibility, and Automation for System Events ().
commands.postcondition: The project folder holds name.xcodeproj and the template's sources; Xcode shows it.

errors.name: ValueError
errors.when: an argument is invalid or mode isn't "ui" or "background"

errors.name: UIError
errors.when: a named element never appeared, or the result wasn't seen in time

errors.name: StateBlocked
errors.when: an Xcode sheet holds typed text or can't be cancelled, or another app came to the front; nothing more was done

errors.name: NotFound
errors.when: the folder, project or template doesn't exist; nothing is done

errors.name: OutsideAllowedRoot
errors.when: XCODE_ALLOWED_ROOT is set and a path is outside it; nothing is done

known_gaps: Verified on macOS 15.6.1 with Xcode 16.4 only, so it isn't known to work on macOS 26 or any other version.
Only touches what XCODE_ALLOWED_ROOT allows if it is set.
It depends on English names and was tested only in English.
Interface, language, testing and storage keep Xcode's defaults (SwiftUI, Swift).
No team is set, so the project isn't signed.
Xcode also rewrites the window-state file (UserInterfaceState.xcuserstate) of projects already open in it.

commands.name: project_build
commands.description: Builds a project with Product > Build for its current scheme and destination, opening it first if Xcode doesn't show it, and reports whether the build succeeded.

args.name: path
args.meaning: The .xcodeproj or .xcworkspace, an absolute path or one starting with ~.

example_requests: Build my Mac app in Xcode
commands.precondition: The program has Accessibility, and Automation for System Events ().
commands.postcondition: Xcode built the scheme; a successful build's app is in Xcode's DerivedData.

errors.name: ValueError
errors.when: an argument is invalid or mode isn't "ui" or "background"

errors.name: UIError
errors.when: a named element never appeared, or the result wasn't seen in time

errors.name: StateBlocked
errors.when: an Xcode sheet holds typed text or can't be cancelled, or another app came to the front; nothing more was done

errors.name: NotFound
errors.when: the folder, project or template doesn't exist; nothing is done

errors.name: OutsideAllowedRoot
errors.when: XCODE_ALLOWED_ROOT is set and a path is outside it; nothing is done

errors.name: NotSupported
errors.when: the scheme needs platform support Xcode would download (it is declined with Cancel), or the mode wasn't verified

known_gaps: Verified on macOS 15.6.1 with Xcode 16.4 only, so it isn't known to work on macOS 26 or any other version.
Only touches what XCODE_ALLOWED_ROOT allows if it is set.
It depends on English names and was tested only in English.
Only macOS App builds were verified; an iOS scheme needed iOS 18.5 support Xcode wanted to download, which is declined.
A failed build returns succeeded false and no products; its errors are in Xcode's Issue navigator.
It waits up to 10 minutes for the build.
